newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Simitis pledges support for Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: Simitis pledges support for Cyprus.

text.p: Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis on Tuesday pledged support for the divided island of Cyprus, with which his nation has a joint defence pact aimed at deterring a perceived threat from Turkey.
"The Cyprus problem is a top priority for Greece in its foreign policy," Simitis said on arrival at Larnaca airport for Cyprus Independence Day celebrations.

Cyprus gained independence from Britain in 1960. In 1974 Turkey invaded the northern side of the island in the wake of a short-lived coup engineerered by the military ruling Greece at the time. Turkey maintains some 30,000 troops in north Cyprus.
Simitis said his visit was an indication of the continuous interest his government has in a just solution of the Cyprus problem and to safeguard the existence of Cypriot Hellenism.

"My visit today on the anniversary of Cyprus independence is because we want to show we support the independence of the Cyprus republic and we want to help it, to assist it in every way to restore its territorial integrity over all Cyprus."

Simitis is on his first visit outside Greece since winning national elections last week. It is the first visit by a Greek prime minister to the east Mediterranean island's independence day celebrations, which include a military parade later on Tuesday.
Simitis was welcomed by President Glafcos Clerides with whom he is expected to discuss the defence pact during his two-day visit.
Clerides on Monday said Cyprus would continue to strengthen defences until a way is found to reunify the country and remove Turkish troops.
